definitions.explanation: A festival celebrated on July 7th (or August 7th in some regions) based on the legend of two star-crossed lovers, Orihime and Hikoboshi, who can meet only once a year across the Milky Way.

examples.japanese: {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りに{行|い}く。
examples.english: To go to the Tanabata festival.

examples.japanese: {仙台|せんだい}の{七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りは{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Sendai's Tanabata festival is the most famous in Japan.

examples.japanese: {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りの{夜|よる}、{子|こ}どもたちが{短冊|たんざく}に{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{書|か}いて{笹|ささ}に{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: On the night of the Tanabata festival, the children wrote their wishes on paper strips and hung them on bamboo branches.

notes:
A compound of {七夕|たなばた} (Tanabata; the seventh evening) and {祭|まつ}り (festival). The festival originates from a Chinese legend about the weaver princess {織姫|おりひめ} (Vega) and the cowherd {彦星|ひこぼし} (Altair), separated by the {天|あま}の{川|がわ} (Milky Way) and allowed to meet only on the seventh day of the seventh month. The most iconic tradition is writing wishes on colorful paper strips ({短冊|たんざく}) and hanging them on bamboo ({笹|ささ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りの{飾|かざ}り: Tanabata decorations
- {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りに{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}をする: to make a wish at Tanabata
- {仙台|せんだい}{七夕祭|たなばたまつ}り: Sendai Tanabata Festival
- {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}りの{短冊|たんざく}: Tanabata wish strips

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {七夕|たなばた}: Tanabata — the day/event itself, without the festival context
- {星祭|ほしまつ}り: Star Festival — an alternative name, emphasizing the celestial legend
- {盆踊|ぼんおど}り: Bon dance festival — another major summer festival, associated with the Obon season
